summary: First source-grounded rank-one checkpoint for R35.1: actual metrized fractional-ideal presentations, local norms, coordinate tensor/dual operations, arithmetic degree, generic-coordinate invariance, quotient degree and the metric-forgetting map. Ordinary ideal theory and the product formula are reused from the pinned library. No Hodge metric, finite-extension theorem, stable Faltings height, isogeny-height estimate or moduli-height comparison is claimed. AI-assisted author: ChatGPT Pro, session cgpt-20260926-6de2, issue #674.

Existing homomorphism from invertible ideals in a chosen fraction field to the ordinary class group.
Comparison with the quotient by principal ideals in the chosen fraction field.
Infinite places from complex embeddings modulo conjugation; a finite index type for number fields.
Multiplicity one at real places and two at complex places.
v(x)>0 exactly when x is nonzero.

The sum of infinite-place multiplicities equals [K:Q].
The product of v(x)^m(v) equals the absolute rational norm of x.

Every infinite place of Q evaluates a rational number by its ordinary absolute value.

nodes.title: Hermitian fractional ideals
hypotheses: K is a number field, R=O_K and d=[K:Q]>0.
Infinite places are indexed modulo conjugation; m(v)=1 at real places and 2 at complex places.
nodes.statement: A Hermitian fractional ideal is a pair L=(I,w), where I is a unit of the existing fractional-ideal ring of R in K and w is a real function on infinite places. This is a coordinate presentation of a metrized rank-one lattice, not yet the category of all metrized invertible sheaves.
proofSteps: Reuse the existing unit group of fractional ideals, so invertibility and nonzeroness are not new axioms.
Store one logarithmic norm scale per infinite place; exp(w(v)) is positive.
Use componentwise equality. Isometry classes are a different, subsequently constructed quotient.
acceptance: Zero fractional ideals are excluded by the carrier.
Changing a logarithmic scale changes the presentation even when the ideal stays fixed.

nodes.title: Local fiber norms

v is an infinite place and z is a complex fiber coordinate.
nodes.statement: Define norm_L,v(z)=exp(w(v))|z|. For x in K, the value on its embedded coordinate is exp(w(v))v(x). There is no multiplicity inside this local complex norm.
proofSteps: Scale the ordinary complex norm by the positive number exp(w(v)).
Use norm_embedding_eq and conjugation invariance to compare the two embeddings of a complex place.
Prove positivity, complex homogeneity and the triangle inequality from the ordinary norm.
acceptance: A complex place contributes weight two to arithmetic degree, not a factor sqrt 2 to this norm.
The scale can be recovered from the norm of 1.

nodes.title: Arithmetic degree
hypotheses: K is a number field, R=O_K, d=[K:Q]; L=(I,w) is a presentation.
m(v)=1 at real places and 2 at complex places; N(I) is the existing fractional-ideal norm.
nodes.statement: Define degHat(L)=-log N(I)-sum_v m(v)w(v), viewing the positive rational norm in R. This degree has not been divided by d.
proofSteps: Use absNorm_nonneg and absNorm_eq_zero_iff to prove that a unit ideal has positive norm.
Take the real logarithm of the existing norm, not of a new ideal invariant.
Use each complex place once, with coefficient two. This is the logarithmic form of the source product-of-scales formula.
acceptance: The finite and infinite contributions have the displayed negative signs.
Do not confuse logarithms of norms with logarithms of squared norms.

nodes.title: Change of generic coordinate
hypotheses: L=(I,w) is over a number field and a belongs to K units; a need not be integral.
nodes.statement: Define reframe_a(L)=(aI,w-log v(a)), using toPrincipalIdeal(a) times I. The coordinate map is x maps to ax. This is D-(a), not D+(a), in the source divisor convention.
proofSteps: Reuse toPrincipalIdeal and its multiplication law.
Every v(a) is positive, so log v(a) is defined with the required nonzero input.
Multiplicativity of v and log of a product give the identity, composition and inverse laws.
acceptance: The log-scale change has a minus sign.
The scalar ranges over K units, not only units of O_K.

Their norms are positive, so the logarithm of the product is the sum of logarithms.

nodes.title: Arithmetic degree is independent of the generic coordinate
hypotheses: K is a number field, L is a presentation and a belongs to K units.
nodes.statement: degHat(reframe_a L)=degHat(L).
proofSteps: coe_toPrincipalIdeal and absNorm_span_singleton give N(aI)=|Norm_K/Q(a)|N(I).
The pinned prod_eq_abs_norm identifies |Norm(a)| with the product of v(a)^m(v). Every factor is positive.
Taking logarithms gives log|Norm(a)|=sum m(v)log v(a). This is an application of the existing formula, not a new product-formula proof.
Substitute into the degree of (aI,w-log v(a)); the two correction sums cancel.
acceptance: The argument works for fractional, not just integral, coordinate changes.
A plus sign in the reframe scale must fail the rational a=2 test.

Its degree is zero, so a second normalization adds zero; degree-zero input is fixed.

gaps.detail: The quotient constructed here is only the scalar-witness quotient of metrized fractional ideals. Prove extension of rank-one module isomorphisms to the generic fiber, recover the placewise metrics and prove essential surjectivity using a generic generator. In a real trace-metric formulation, u_v=sqrt(<e_v,e_v>/m(v)); the uncorrected p.454 formula fails at complex places. gaps.detail: The section formula needs a finite quotient and #(I/Rs)=|Norm(s)|/N(I) for nonzero s in I. Extension needs N_L(I O_L)=N_K(I)^[L:K] and the weighted count of infinite places above each v. Defining normalizedDegree proves none of these statements; no extension invariance is claimed.

sourceIssues.locator: Published p.452, Proposition 3.1 equality clause; also arXiv v1 p.5

sourceIssues.correction: Equality holds exactly when all |uσ| are equal, equivalently u conjugate(u) is in the diagonal nonnegative real subalgebra. It does not require equal phases or signs of u itself.
